title: The Carboxyl Group: Structure and Naming
subject: Chemistry
objective: What –COOH really is: a carbonyl and a hydroxyl on one sp² carbon, joined by resonance that makes the carbon less electrophilic than in aldehydes; and how carboxylic acids get their common and IUPAC names.

fill.q: The carboxyl group is a carbonyl group plus a ____ group.
The IUPAC name of HCOOH is ____ acid.

tf.q: The carboxyl carbon is more electrophilic than an aldehyde's carbonyl carbon.
tf.explain: Resonance with the –OH lone pair makes it less electrophilic.

tf.q: Acetic acid takes its name from vinegar.
In naming acids, the COOH carbon is C-1.
tf.explain: Numbering starts at the carboxyl carbon.

ar.a: Carboxylic acids do not give the nucleophilic addition reactions of aldehydes.
ar.r: Resonance makes the carboxyl carbon less electrophilic.

mcq.explain: Three-carbon chain from the COOH carbon, methyl on C-2.

num.q: How many carbons are in the parent chain of 2-methylpropanoic acid?

short.q: Show with curved arrows the resonance in the carboxyl group.
short.solution: R–C(=O)–OH ⟷ R–C(–O⁻)=O⁺–H: an –OH lone pair moves into the C–O bond; the C=O π pair moves onto O.

match.explain: Each formula matches its IUPAC name.
